title: Chunk-aware attention runner and adaptive decode scheduler for v2/v3 stability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Since onboarding FlashAttention v3 we observed increased decode jitter and occasional regressions on long-context workloads when the kernel selector oscillates between v2 and v3 implementations during prefill->decode transitions. This ticket implements a chunk-aware attention runner and an adaptive decode scheduler to stabilize kernel handoffs and reduce tail latency.
goal: Eliminate kernel oscillation during startup and prefill->decode boundary for long-context (>=8k tokens) sessions; reduce p95 decode latency by >=15% on affected workloads; keep model output parity within existing QA thresholds.
success_criteria: kernel_switch_rate <= 0.5 switches/min per worker under mixed traffic
decode_latency_p95 reduced by >=15% on long-context replay workload
no regressions detected in the automated regression-eval suite (prompt set: reg-2026-attn-longcontexts)
KV cache hit rate maintained or improved (no more than 2% drop)
deployable canary with traffic mirror and automatic rollback hooks
plan: 1) Implement chunk-aware attention runner: runtime will expose per-request chunking hints to the kernel selector so kernels are chosen with chunk boundaries in mind. 2) Adaptive decode scheduler: introduce a short holdback window (~2-4 tokens) at prefill->decode transition to allow v3 layout warmup, with dynamic shortening based on recent stability signals. 3) Telemetry: add kernel_switch_rate, chunk_mismatch_count, decode_hold_time_histogram. 4) Canary: traffic mirror 5% of traffic for three hours; run the regression-eval harness and human-in-the-loop checks. 5) Rollout: staged 10/30/60 with rollback automation tied to p95 and error rate thresholds.
work_items: implement chunk hint API in runtime (libruntime/attn/chunk_hints.cc)
kernel selector changes to respect chunk affinity and avoid oscillation (serving/kernels/selector.cpp)
adaptive holdback scheduler and config flags (serving/schedulers/decode_scheduler.cc)
add telemetry collectors and Grafana dashboards (telemetry/attn-kernel-metrics)
integration tests and regression-eval suite update (tests/regressions/long_contexts)
create canary pipeline with traffic mirror and rollback (infra/canaries/attn-chunk-aware)
run controlled load tests on dedicated infra (dedicated/stress/longctx)
PR review and post-deploy monitoring plan
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: holdback window increases latency for short requests. Mitigation: dynamic shortening based on recent kernel stability metrics and request length heuristic.
Risk: chunk hints might be ignored by some kernels causing mismatch. Mitigation: fallback path that forces a single kernel for the session and records telemetry for debugging.
Risk: regressions in output quality from different kernel numerical behaviour. Mitigation: run regression-eval suite and prompt-level diffing; option to pin model to v2 for specific customers.
Risk: rollout causing capacity pressure on Dedicated clusters. Mitigation: limit canary to hosted regions and dedicated staging clusters first; autoscaling knobs and pre-warm capacity reserved.
testing_plan: Unit tests for chunk hint propagation, integration tests for prefill->decode boundary, synthetic replay harness with long-context prompts, and golden-output comparison. Canary run: 5% mirrored traffic with automated regression-eval every 30 minutes and human review at 2 hours.
telemetry_and_dashboards: New metrics: kernel_switch_rate (per-worker), chunk_affinity_miss, decode_hold_time_ms_hist, kv_cache_hit_rate_by_chunk. Dashboards: Attn Kernel Stability (p50/p95 latency, error rate, switch rate), Canary Healthboard. Alerts: kernel_switch_rate > 1/min sustained for 5m, decode_p95 increase >20% vs baseline.
rollout_strategy: Canary mirror 5% -> staged 10%/30%/60% with 30m observation windows and automated rollback on threshold breaches. For Dedicated customers, opt-in via config flag and manual approval.

notes: This approach seeks to reduce brittle kernel switching by making the selector chunk-aware and by softening the prefill->decode transition. It is intentionally conservative: default holdback is small and dynamic; operators can tune aggressiveness per-deployment.
